transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I came in because things suddenly got kind of intense. I’d just moved into a new apartment and I was barely even unpacked, like there are still boxes by the wall, and then all at once I started saying yes to everything—mentoring sessions, extra client prototypes, redoing my whole design portfolio.

It was like I had to fix my entire life in one sprint, if that makes sense. Which is funny because in interface design sprints are supposed to be structured, but this felt more like I couldn’t stop adding tasks to the board. So… yeah, that shift is what made me think maybe I should talk to someone.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like needing less sleep or feeling rested with very little sleep?

Yeah, sleep got weird. For several nights I was only sleeping maybe three or four hours, but I’d wake up like, “Great, I’m fine, I should just use this time and get ahead.” Which is not normally me—I usually need more sleep.

And then I’d be up thinking about what I could finish before the day even started, like reorganizing files or tweaking portfolio pages, and suddenly it’s 5 a.m. and I’m acting like that’s productive instead of… probably not great.
Have you been having trouble slowing down or felt the need to keep going with projects even when you know you should rest?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, I would tell myself I was just “getting organized,” but there were nights where I couldn’t sit still at all. I’d be moving furniture around, then labeling storage bins, then suddenly I’d be back at my computer tweaking mockups.

And it wasn’t even like one project, it was everything. I’d pace around the apartment looking for the next thing to fix, because stopping felt… impossible. Like if I sat down, I was wasting time or something.
Have you noticed your mood being unusually high, overly confident, or excessively optimistic during these periods of increased activity?

Yeah… I think so. Earlier this month I had these moments where I felt almost electric, like everything was going to work out and I could just push through anything.

But then it would flip really fast. Like, if a contractor was late getting back to me about some apartment thing, or my sister didn’t answer a text right away, I’d get weirdly sharp with them—like these tiny delays were some huge personal obstacle. And then later I’d be like, why did I make that such a big deal?
Have you noticed yourself being more talkative than usual, interrupting others more often, or feeling like you needed to keep talking because your thoughts were racing?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think I’ve noticed myself talking more than usual in a clear way. Like, I can be chatty if I’m excited about a design thing, or if someone asks me about a website flow I’ll go on too long—my friends would probably say I already do that sometimes.

But interrupting people or feeling like I have to keep talking because I can’t stop my thoughts… I don’t know. I haven’t really clocked that specifically. Maybe I’d have to ask someone close to me, because I might not notice it in the moment.
Has there been a time when your energy or activity level got so intense that it caused serious problems at work, in your relationships, or made you unable to function normally without help?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d say “unable to function” exactly, but it has caused problems.

I missed a design review, which is… really not like me, or at least I don’t want it to be like me. I had all these files open and I was trying to make everything perfect, and then somehow I just—missed the actual meeting. Which sounds so stupid when I say it out loud.

And I’ve been kind of avoiding people since then. Friends, my family… my sister especially. Not because they did anything, just because I feel embarrassed. Like I’ve seemed so scattered and unreliable lately, and I don’t really want to explain that.

Have you ever had a period where your mood was really elevated or you felt extremely energetic, and it was so intense that others around you noticed you were acting out of character or you had to be hospitalized?

I don’t think it got to the level of… like, a hospital or anything like that. But earlier this month, yeah, I was definitely not quite myself.

I had these stretches where I felt almost electric, really upbeat, like I could handle everything at once. And then something tiny would happen—like a contractor taking too long to respond, or my sister not texting back right away—and I’d snap, like they were personally getting in my way. Which, looking back, is kind of embarrassing because it was just normal life stuff.
Have you had a period where your mood was so elevated, irritable, or you felt so energetic that it lasted most of the day, nearly every day, for at least four days in a row?

Earlier this month is the closest thing to that, yeah. I don’t know if I’m counting the days correctly—like, I wasn’t marking it on a calendar—but there was definitely a stretch where I felt almost electric, really upbeat, like everything was suddenly doable.

And then it would flip into me being really irritable. Like a contractor would take too long to respond, or my sister wouldn’t text back, and I’d react like they were personally trying to block me or slow me down. Which sounds dramatic now, but in the moment it felt very real. So… yes, there was a period like that, I’m just not totally sure about the exact number of days.
Can you confirm if there was a clear period where your mood was consistently elevated or irritable, lasting at least four days in a row?

Yeah… I think so. Earlier this month there was a clear stretch where I felt almost electric, like weirdly upbeat and charged up, and then I’d turn around and get really irritated over small things.

Like a contractor taking too long to answer, or my sister not texting back, and I’d react like they were deliberately blocking me somehow. Which is embarrassing, because normally I can wait for an email without making it into a whole thing. So… yes, I’d say it was a few days in a row, at least.
